## A Practical Synthesis Without a Swing Prescription {#sec-lay-ch28}

## A Concrete Picture

A weather map connects pressure, wind and uncertainty without deciding whether
every person should carry an umbrella. The decision also depends on the journey
and the consequences of getting wet. A swing model has a similar role: it can
explain a mechanism and predict a conditional outcome without establishing one
motion as best for every golfer.

The useful synthesis connects several questions that are easy to confuse.
Geometry helps determine how forces affect motion. Force and application-point velocity jointly determine power. Work changes the selected system's energy, but an energy total
does not uniquely determine clubhead speed. Many hand-force allocations can
produce the same club wrench (resultant force and moment), while requiring
different internal loads. The
controls that create a useful state must also be feasible before that state is
reached. Each connection needs its own evidence.

![A Conceptual Review Map Connects Energy, Geometry, Timing, Robustness, Human Evidence and Falsification; It Does Not Assign Equal Support to Every Claim.](figures/proximal_distal_companion/fig_companion_synthesis_map.svg){#fig-lay-synthesis width=98% fig-alt="Six review topics surround a testable mechanism. Arrows connect questions to investigate rather than showing measured causal effects or equal evidence strength."}

## How the Mechanism Works

### Begin With the Claim, System and Comparison

A useful claim specifies the system, outcome, intervention, comparison and range
of conditions. Club kinetic energy, clubhead speed, face orientation, joint load
and repeatability are different outcomes. An improvement in one need not improve
the others. Define the event too: a fixed simulation time or a club-angle
crossing is not a resolved ball collision.

Choose a boundary before identifying an energy source. Hand forces can do work
on the club while transferring energy internally when the arms and club are
considered together. Muscle action can convert chemical energy into mechanical
energy inside that larger system. An ideal stationary ground contact can
exchange momentum without doing mechanical work; a moving or compliant
boundary needs its own power and storage terms. The words *proximal* and
*distal* describe location, not a guaranteed one-way energy flow.

Next state what was measured and what was inferred. A model state can include
configuration, velocity, shaft deformation and actuator memory. Knowing one
angle, one speed peak or one scalar energy total does not reconstruct that
state. Unmeasured states and uncertain parameters must remain visible in the
interpretation.

### Connect Force, Moment and Power Before Interpreting Signs

For a rigid club, hand action can be reduced to a resultant force
$\mathbf F$ and moment $\mathbf M_C$ about its center of mass $C$. Its
instantaneous hand-to-club power is

$$
P_{\mathrm{hands}\to\mathrm{club}}
=\mathbf F\cdot\mathbf v_C+\mathbf M_C\cdot\boldsymbol\omega.
$$

Here $\mathbf v_C$ is center-of-mass velocity and $\boldsymbol\omega$ is
club angular velocity in the declared frame. Include both force-generated
moments and any direct grip moments in $\mathbf M_C$. This is the same power
obtained by summing the individual hand forces dotted with their application-
point velocities, plus the direct moments dotted with angular velocity.

A negative component of moment is a direction relative to a chosen axis. Its
power also depends on the conjugate motion. Even negative rotational power can
coexist with positive total hand-to-club power through the force term. Neither
sign alone identifies which muscle worked, whether a golfer was passive, or
whether the action improved a later outcome. See @sec-lay-ch13 for the separate
questions hidden inside “negative torque.”

Consider an explicitly manufactured planar example. Grip positions relative to
$C$ are $(0,0.1)$ and $(0,-0.1)\,\mathrm m$. Hand forces are
$(10,20)$ and $(-10,30)\,\mathrm N$. Their resultant is
$(0,50)\,\mathrm N$, and their summed moment about $C$ is
$-2\,\mathrm{N\,m}$ under the positive out-of-plane convention. With
$\mathbf v_C=(2,1)\,\mathrm{m/s}$ and angular velocity
$+3\,\mathrm{rad/s}$ about that axis, translational power is $50\,\mathrm W$ and rotational
power is $-6\,\mathrm W$. The club receives $44\,\mathrm W$ in total.
The two application-point velocities are $(1.7,1)$ and
$(2.3,1)\,\mathrm{m/s}$, giving individual powers $37$ and $7\,\mathrm W$.

This identity is a bookkeeping check, not evidence that these loads occur in a
golfer. If the shaft deforms, a single rigid-body twist no longer describes all
its points. If an interface slips or deforms, use the relevant velocities and
account for interface storage and dissipation. Do not force a flexible or
slipping system into the rigid-club shortcut.

### The Same Club Wrench Can Hide Different Hand Demands

In that example, add $(0,100)\,\mathrm N$ to the first force and subtract it
from the second. The added forces are equal, opposite and collinear with the
line between the grips. They change neither the resultant force nor the moment
about $C$. The total power remains $44\,\mathrm W$, but the individual powers
become $137$ and $-93\,\mathrm W$.

This is a null direction of the wrench map: a change in force allocation that
the net wrench cannot reveal. It can alter internal loading and power exchange
between the hands even when the club's instantaneous net action is unchanged.
It does not follow that every such allocation is physically admissible. Under
an illustrative per-hand force limit of $50\,\mathrm N$, the first allocation
satisfies the limit and the modified allocation violates it. That limit is a
manufactured constraint, not a measured human strength threshold.

Contact friction, grip capacity, joint limits, actuator bounds and state history
restrict the feasible allocations. Adding muscles introduces further unknowns
rather than automatically identifying one solution. Matching a net club wrench
is weaker than matching the complete trajectory, contact states and biological
demands. Distinguish these comparisons before interpreting a push--pull strategy
or attributing a club moment to the trail hand alone.

### Equal Energy Is Not Equal Clubhead Speed

For a rigid body, velocity at a head point $H$ is

$$
\mathbf v_H=\mathbf v_C+\boldsymbol\omega\times\mathbf r_{H/C}.
$$

The translational and rotational contributions can reinforce or oppose one
another. In a second manufactured example, take a planar rigid body of mass
$1\,\mathrm{kg}$, central rotational inertia $0.25\,\mathrm{kg\,m^2}$,
$\mathbf v_C=(0,2)\,\mathrm{m/s}$ and
$\mathbf r_{H/C}=(0.5,0)\,\mathrm m$. Angular velocities of
$+2$ and $-2\,\mathrm{rad/s}$ give the same kinetic energy,
$2.5\,\mathrm J$, but head speeds of $3$ and $1\,\mathrm{m/s}$.

These are instantaneous states at the same pose. They do not prove that both
are reachable from one initial state under the same torque or grip limits.
They show why a scalar energy budget cannot replace the geometry and velocity
information needed for a task. In a linked swing, initial energy, subsequent
work, dissipation and redistribution all matter. The useful question is how a
feasible trajectory places motion and energy at the required task event, while
also meeting face/path, impact and load constraints.

### Compare Interventions at the Right Level

Pointwise attribution holds the complete state fixed and changes a declared
input or model term. Recompute the constraint reactions under that change. A
forward branch copies the complete initial state and then evolves under its
own inputs and reactions. A preparation study changes the history that creates
that state. A policy comparison may additionally retune the controls. These
answer different questions; none substitutes automatically for another.

Copy actuator, controller and flexible states as well as angles and velocities.
A zero command need not remove a stored actuator load, and zero direct wrist
torque need not remove force-generated moment or interface power. If a
zero-velocity diagnostic is used, it changes the state and must satisfy the
retained boundary conditions. The discussions in @sec-lay-ch11 and
@sec-lay-ch18 explain these distinctions.

Matching peak torque, impulse, mechanical work and endpoint task are also
different controls on an experiment. State which quantities are matched and
which are allowed to change. A later benefit does not by itself show that early
negative work was its cause. Compare the relevant alternatives, including
failures and admissible negative controls.

A clock trigger and a measured-state trigger should be compared using declared
sensors, noise, latency and control limits. Aligning a finished swing by its
actual future impact is a retrospective analysis, not information a real-time
controller already possesses. A force-direction or moment-arm reversal with
forces held fixed is an algebraic geometry test; changing the geometry and
re-solving a forward trajectory need not reverse its resultant moment.

### What the Current Model Comparisons Support

The pinned research record contains several distinct tests, not one model
validated at every level. Planar two-hand forward branches examine finite
persistence after selected applied torques are removed. Coupled moving-base and
shaft models examine additional physical pathways. A common-state spatial
comparison tests prescribed-force geometry and rigid-body dynamics. The reduced
spatial forward-contact comparison uses hand carriages, shared compliant
interfaces and a shared state update; its agreement is not independent contact-
solver validation or proof for articulated human arms.

The same record includes adverse results and unresolved boundaries. A
preregistered finite-base comparison did not obtain its required matched-load
and dissipation conditions. A contact-geometry audit showed why full rank does
not establish that anatomically placed hands actually meet the club grips. Later closed-state screens and short-horizon
trajectory checks answer narrower questions than a complete calibrated swing.
Treat each result according to its model, intervention, observable and tested
range, as the reviewer workbench specifies.

The saved uncertainty/control comparison tests eight prescribed programs on six
training and six held-out model parameter draws. Independently recomputing
nondominance from its saved summary rows gives seven nondominated programs on
the training ensemble and all eight on the held-out ensemble. A program is
nondominated within that set if no other tested program is at least as good on
every declared objective and strictly better on at least one.

The objectives reward the tenth-percentile delivery speed ($\mathrm{m/s}$)
while penalizing mean absolute planar face-to-path angle error (degrees),
90th-percentile hand force ($\mathrm N$), squared-torque effort and delivery
speed standard deviation ($\mathrm{m/s}$). The “effort” integral has units
$(\mathrm{N\,m})^2\mathrm s$; it is neither mechanical work nor metabolic cost.
Delivery is evaluated at a fixed model time without ball collision. The
parameter ranges are engineering assumptions, and tail statistics from six
draws are not calibrated population quantiles. This chapter checks stored
summaries, not a new dynamics run.

Those results show tradeoffs among the tested programs. They do not prove that
no untested policy can improve all five outcomes. For a simple two-objective
illustration in which smaller is better, $(1,4)$ and $(4,1)$ are nondominated
relative to each other, yet an additional feasible result $(0.5,0.5)$ would
improve both. Whether such an alternative is actually attainable requires a
separate analysis. Nor does a choice of objective weights identify a golfer's
control objective.

### Keep the Strategy Families as Testable Hypotheses

One proposed family emphasizes arm-side drive with early wrist resistance;
another emphasizes a different phase allocation of wrist drive and arm
resistance. Preserve both as hypotheses about inputs, state preparation and
outcomes. They are not exhaustive biological categories, and a generalized
actuator subspace is not an identified shoulder-girdle muscle group.

Define *preload* as the load already present at a declared initial state, and
*slack* as motion before a specified resistance engages. Use *transmission gap*
only with an operational definition, such as a stated clearance or response
delay; those mechanisms are not interchangeable.
A force crossing zero need not mean that contact opened. A compliant element
can remain engaged at low force; low tangent stiffness, clearance, contact
separation and actuator delay are different mechanisms. Continued command does
not guarantee immediate delivered load, and reversing a command does not
necessarily erase stored load. The declared transmission law and initial state
determine the prediction.

A fair test examines feasible preparation, bilateral wrenches, contact state,
work and outcomes across a declared range. It may find a benefit, a cost, no
resolvable difference or a failure of the proposed mechanism. Do not assume in
advance that an opposing moment stabilizes the swing or that a longer retained
configuration must improve delivery. “Manage the negative couple” becomes a
scientific claim only after the measurable intervention and outcome are named.

### Measurements Constrain Models Without Identifying Everything

Synchronized kinematics, external wrenches and inertial assumptions can support
net dynamic estimates with propagated uncertainty. Missing forces, uncertain
segment properties and numerical differentiation can change those estimates.
Bilateral grip sensing can distinguish allocations hidden by the net wrench,
provided its measured components, calibration, frames and timing are adequate.
Shaft strain constrains deformation only through a declared structural and
sensor model; a gauge is not a direct measurement of all stored elastic energy.

Surface EMG records electrical activity associated with muscle-fibre excitation.
Its amplitude is not a direct measurement of activation, force or work; geometry,
recording conditions and excitation-to-force dynamics affect interpretation
[@vigotsky2018EMG]. Perturbation responses can constrain mechanical impedance,
but stiffness, damping, inertia and delayed feedback require an identified model
and a declared perturbation range. These measurements can discriminate among
hypotheses without uniquely recovering every biological state.

**Model Result:** The project supplies conditional mechanism tests and numerical
checks with different scopes. Some comparisons support a bounded pathway;
others expose a failed match or an unresolved inference.

**Human Evidence:** The cited measurement literature constrains interpretation.
The research record's synthetic protocol checks are readiness evidence, not
human observations validating the complete strategy.

**Hypothesis:** A feasible choice of arm/wrist allocation and preparation may
improve a specified combination of delivery, load and repeatability outcomes.
Which choice, for whom and over what conditions remains an experimental question.

**Practical Interpretation:** Use the framework to formulate a comparison and
decide what evidence is missing, rather than converting a model label into a cue.

### A Research Workflow That Can Change Its Mind

Write the prediction and failure rule before choosing the preferred result.
Select the smallest model that can represent the disputed mechanism: a linked
chain for inertial coupling, bilateral contacts for hand allocation, flexible
states for shaft behavior, a moving base for boundary work, or spatial dynamics
for out-of-plane effects. More detail does not automatically strengthen evidence;
each addition needs verified equations, consistent state and suitable data.

Check numerical convergence over a declared range, contact feasibility and
physical work separately from numerical corrections. Compare independent
implementations using matched physical definitions, and identify any shared
contact or integration code. Small residuals verify aspects of a calculation;
they do not validate every assumption about a golfer.

When a prediction fails, inspect synchronization, frames, parameters, numerical
error and observation uncertainty. If a discrepancy remains outside the declared
range, reject or revise the specific model-and-measurement claim. A failed
anatomical mapping can invalidate the application of otherwise correct contact
mechanics. A failed wrench prediction does not overturn Newton's laws. Keep
adverse results rather than changing the outcome or tolerance after seeing them.

Reserve participants or conditions for predictions made without tuning on them.
A held-out synthetic draw checks robustness within an assumed model family; a
held-out participant checks a different external generalization. Report what
was fitted, what was fixed, which data were withheld and which claims remain
unidentified.

### A Reader's Next Experiment

Translate “trail-hand pull creates passive wrist lag and more speed” into
separate propositions. Define the force components and moment point, define lag
as a measured state variable, name the supposedly passive input channel and
choose the delivery outcome. Ask whether another hand allocation or preparation
history can reproduce the observations. Then predict discriminating wrenches,
powers, deformation or responses under a feasible comparison.

The linked workbench is a place to inspect available model controls and their
limitations. At the [pinned catalog revision](https://github.com/D-sorganization/Tools/blob/cefcc1878de11804c44cd7d1d19c0ffcf58fa89e/src/pendulum_simulator/src/double_pendulum_golf/resources/companion_catalog.json), the desktop Companion Guide displays
experiment instructions; the React guide can select a model and display the
shared instructions. A catalog workflow is not by itself evidence that every
step is implemented as a runnable experiment. Check the version and the actual
controls before promising clock/state comparisons, shaft changes or a copied-
state branch in a particular interface. Use a recorded script when an experiment
requires capabilities beyond that interface. No new frontend run is certified
by this chapter.

Predict the result first, retain failed cases, and inspect force, power, work,
contact and uncertainty alongside final speed. Promote exploratory output only
with reproducible inputs, declared numerical checks and traceable interpretation.

### What Completion Should Mean

The desired product connects readable explanations, auditable derivations,
versioned simulations, qualified measurements and reproducible publication.
Readers should be able to move from a claim to its assumptions, evidence and
possible refutation. Completing that framework does not mean proving a
preferred biological strategy or making every proposed experiment available in
every interface.

Priorities follow the unresolved question: feasible articulated contact before
interpreting its loads, equipment calibration before equipment-specific
predictions, and prospective human tests before individual recommendations.
The evidence may change the proposed mechanism or favor a competing allocation.
A synthesis is useful when it makes that revision possible.

## Where the Picture Breaks

The map can make every connection look equally established. Mechanical
identities, manufactured examples, finite simulation results, human observations
and hypotheses have different evidentiary roles. Preserve those labels when a
passage or figure is quoted outside the book.

Uncertainty should not erase conditional predictions. State them precisely and
test them within their declared scope. Neither numerical agreement nor a
persuasive mechanism establishes a universally superior swing, a particular
scapular action or a safe loading prescription.
